label: Game B
nuance_found: Tap the handbrake into a corner to start a drift, steer into the slide, chain drifts for a multiplier; smashing bollards, signs and lamp posts pays far more than clean driving (SMASH x2 to x7, up to +3,590). I did not find a real trade-off, and hitting things seemed to be the best way to score.
audio: No music at all. Engine and wind drones that rise and fall with speed, tyre noise, a metallic crash thud, bright pickup chimes for bollards and smashes, a tick when time is added. It sounded like a toy engine, not a tune.
furthest_progress: Yozakura Pass, Easy: drove from 17:20 golden hour to 01:33 at night (about 40 mi on the trip counter) in one run, score about 16,270, combo never above x2, no clear end or finish seen.
control_trouble: Thumb stick is very twitchy and I only see the screen every 0.5 s, so I could not hold the road on bends. I think a real thumb would do better, but small steering inputs still spun the car. Holding the finger down for gas and tapping the handbrake with a second finger worked.
best_moment: Plowing through a row of bollards in the tunnel for a SMASH x7 +3,590 with a rush of chimes, at sunset with petals falling.
worst_moment: Driving into a tree or guardrail and being stuck at 0 mph for 8 to 10 s waiting for the magnet to pull me back, over and over; camera also gets buried inside tree canopies and I cannot see anything.
verdict: Gorgeous little thing, the sunset and rain and neon are lovely, and the first minute of just driving and smashing signs felt nice. But I never really knew what I was meant to win. There is a clock and a score but no target and no level, and driving well pays almost nothing while crashing pays loads, which feels backwards. I spent most of my time stuck on a verge waiting for the magnet. I would try it once for the looks and delete it after the bus ride.
